edges.description: Expressed in cultured endothelial cells and melanocytes, the mutant made the cells independent of growth factors by upregulating MAPK signalling; the steps from there to the tumour's lymphatic-type endothelium are not established. A later series found no GNA14 mutation in five further KHEs, and the 2020 review leaves open whether such mutations cause the tumour.

The nodules infiltrate across tissue planes, into the dermis, fat, muscle and bone. In mouse haemangioendothelioma cells, overexpression of PROX1 induced an invasive phenotype in vivo, a model of a link between the lymphatic programme and infiltration rather than a study of human tumours.
In most patients the infiltrating tumour presents as a soft-tissue mass with skin findings.
Pain can come from the infiltrating, destructive growth.
The infiltrating tumour invades the joints near it.

In a cohort selected for loss of joint motion, most limb lesions were on or next to large joints. The cohort calls the cause uncertain and, citing earlier work, states that infiltration of muscle, connective tissue and joint structures can lead to fibrosis and contracture.
The tumour invades and destroys bone.

Lymphoedema can follow the tumour, more often when it is large (10 cm or more), mixed and in a limb. On lymphoscintigraphy of 25 patients, 24 of them with a limb tumour, lymphatic stasis within the involved lesion was found in all 22 with abnormal findings, and lymphoedema was on the side of the lesion, as it was in all 13 affected patients of the cohort of 118. The 2020 review suggests that a tumour of the proximal limb, particularly at or near the inguinal or axillary lymph nodes, may influence lymphatic development or damage the lymphatic vessels, and reports a hypothesis that, for such tumours, obstruction of lymphatic flow during the acute Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon may lead to lymphoedema; it adds that inflammation may also play a role. In the cohort of 118, of whom 13 had lymphoedema, a history of the phenomenon and sirolimus treatment were not significant predictors of lymphoedema; with 13 cases this does not exclude them. The lymphoscintigraphy series' abstract names no centre, so whether it shares patients with the cohort of 118 is not known.
The tumour vasculature traps platelets. Infiltration into muscle or deeper, and a retroperitoneal or intrathoracic site, are associated with a higher likelihood of the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon.
Trapping and consumption of platelets lowers the platelet count.

Anaemia accompanies the falling platelet count of the phenomenon. The cited sources name the anaemia of the phenomenon as microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia, and intralesional haemorrhage among its consequences, without tracing the steps from trapping to anaemia.

nodes.description: The tumour grows as infiltrating nodules of spindled endothelial cells lining slit-like or crescentic vessels. The endothelium stains for CD31 and CD34 and for the lymphatic markers LYVE1, PROX1 and podoplanin (D2-40), and not for GLUT-1. Angiogenesis and lymphangiogenesis are dysregulated and progressive. How fast the endothelium proliferates is not settled: the cohort of 70 reports Ki-67 on the endothelial cells, while in the lesion the 2020 review illustrates only a few nuclei stained for it. The 2020 review adds VEGFR-3 to these lymphatic markers; in a thoracic series of 7 KHEs and 6 kaposiform lymphangiomatoses, all lesions examined had spindle tumour cells staining for CD31 and D2-40, and CD31-positive cells isolated from three of six patients' tumours carried CD31, Ki-67 and LYVE1 in culture. Which signals drive the programme is not established. The review suggests, from the expression of both in KHE, that the VEGF-C/VEGFR3 axis may contribute to the tumour's aggressive behaviour, while serum VEGF-C was lower in KHE patients with the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon, a different compartment from the tissue, against a comparison group the abstract does not state. Serum angiopoietin-2 was 14-fold raised in KHE when the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon was present and not when it was absent, and the serum study proposes it, with the angiopoietin-1 that was lower alongside VEGF-C, as a marker of the phenomenon's coagulopathy. The review offers vascular remodelling, such as vessel sprouting and inflammatory lymphangiogenesis, as a possible explanation of the rise, raises the possibility of a paracrine effect on the tumour's endothelial cells, and also raises the possibility of a role for angiopoietin-2 in the phenomenon itself.

nodes.description: An mTOR inhibitor. In a randomised trial in KHE with the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon, in which sirolimus was given for at least 12 months, adding a short course of prednisolone raised the week-4 platelet response from 24 of 36 to 35 of 37; in a randomised trial in KHE without the phenomenon, low-dose sirolimus was non-inferior to high-dose at one year (about 90% response in both); in a cohort of 167 patients, 92.2% had a durable response. On dose, a series of 21 patients, started on sirolimus alone at 0.8 mg/m2 twice a day once there was no sign of the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon aiming for a trough of 5 to 20 ng/mL, found faster tumour shrinkage above a trough of 10 ng/mL and no further gain above 15, in groups of 8, 7 and 6 patients; the randomised trial in KHE without the phenomenon found a trough of 5 to 8 ng/mL non-inferior to 10 to 15 for a volume reduction of at least 20% at month 12, with similar total and serious adverse events but fewer respiratory, skin and mucosal ones. In a pharmacokinetic model of 17 children aged 0.2 to 6 years, the drug's apparent clearance rose with age and was higher in boys than in girls of the same age, which the authors put down to body weight. In the patients with the phenomenon in a 52-patient series, tumour shrinkage did not differ significantly between the 21 given short-term prednisolone for severe symptoms and those on sirolimus alone, whereas the randomised prednisolone trial in KHE with the phenomenon reported better objective lesion responses at month 12 with it. On stopping, rebound growth followed discontinuation in 17.3% of the patients of the cohort of 167 who stopped sirolimus (the abstract does not say how many stopped), associated with early discontinuation and with mixed lesion type, for which the abstract's own confidence interval includes 1; in a series of 26, 25 of them with the phenomenon, 20 completed a course of 28.3 months on average, and the series had no recurrence over a median follow-up of 32 months (the abstract does not say whether follow-up ran from the start or the end of treatment). In the cohort of 167, nonresponse, relapse and long-term sequelae remained despite intensified and prolonged treatment. On harms, serious adverse events were most common in the first year and long-term treatment brought no unacceptable cumulative toxicity in that cohort; in the randomised prednisolone trial, total and grade 3-4 adverse events were similar with and without prednisolone; no patient in the 52-patient series stopped permanently for toxicity, and the 26-patient series reported mild side effects; and a 4-month-old on sirolimus and a prednisolone taper developed Pneumocystis pneumonia with respiratory failure needing extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, after which the authors advise considering prophylaxis.

evidence.reference_title: Population pharmacokinetics of sirolimus in pediatric patients with kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: A retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: Age, alanine transaminase levels and sex were included as significant covariates for CL/F, while the duration of treatment with sirolimus was a significant covariate for V/F.

evidence.reference_title: Population pharmacokinetics of sirolimus in pediatric patients with kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: A retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: The present study indicated that CL/F increased with age, and that males had a higher CL/F than females of the same age. This was expected, as infants/children gain weight as their age increases, and males have a higher body weight than females.

evidence.reference_title: Sirolimus for the treatment of progressive kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: A multicenter retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: For subgroup analysis of KMP patients, there were no significant differences in tumor shrinkage between those treated with combination therapy and those receiving sirolimus alone (95% CI, 18.11-25.02; p > 0.05).

evidence.reference_title: Sirolimus for the treatment of progressive kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: A multicenter retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: Patients without KMP were all treated with sirolimus alone, whereas 21 KMP patients with severe symptoms received short-term combination therapy with prednisolone.

evidence.reference_title: Sirolimus plus prednisolone vs sirolimus monotherapy for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: a randomized clinical trial
evidence.snippet: Compared with the sirolimus monotherapy group, the combination treatment group showed improvements in terms of measures of durable platelet responses at all points during the initial 3-week treatment period, median platelet counts during weeks 1 to 4, increased numbers of patients achieving fibrinogen stabilization at week 4, and objective lesion responses at month 12.

evidence.reference_title: Long‐term outcomes of sirolimus treatment for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: Continuing successes and ongoing challenges
evidence.snippet: Rebound growth occurred in 17.3% of patients upon sirolimus discontinuation.

evidence.reference_title: Long‐term outcomes of sirolimus treatment for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: Continuing successes and ongoing challenges
evidence.snippet: Early treatment discontinuation (odds ratio [OR]: 3.103; 95% CI: 1.529‐6.299; P = .002) and mixed lesion type (OR: 2.271; 95% CI: 0.901‐5.727; P = .047) were associated with tumor rebound growth.

evidence.reference_title: Sirolimus therapy for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma with long-term follow-up.
evidence.snippet: Twenty patients completed sirolimus therapy in 28.3 ± 12.5 months.

evidence.reference_title: Sirolimus therapy for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma with long-term follow-up.
evidence.snippet: Twenty-five patients had Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon (KMP).

evidence.reference_title: Sirolimus therapy for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma with long-term follow-up.
evidence.snippet: The median follow-up time was 32 months (26-60 months), with no evidence of recurrences.

evidence.reference_title: Long‐term outcomes of sirolimus treatment for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: Continuing successes and ongoing challenges
evidence.snippet: Serious adverse events occurred most commonly during the first year of sirolimus therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Long‐term outcomes of sirolimus treatment for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: Continuing successes and ongoing challenges
evidence.snippet: Follow‐up of almost 4.5 years demonstrated that the efficacy of sirolimus persisted over time and that long‐term treatment with sirolimus was not associated with unacceptable cumulative toxicities.

evidence.reference_title: Long‐term outcomes of sirolimus treatment for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: Continuing successes and ongoing challenges
evidence.snippet: However, nonresponse, tumor relapse and long‐term sequelae remained challenges despite intensified and prolonged sirolimus therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Sirolimus plus prednisolone vs sirolimus monotherapy for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: a randomized clinical trial
evidence.snippet: The frequencies of total adverse events and grade 3-4 adverse events during treatment were similar in both groups.

evidence.reference_title: Sirolimus for the treatment of progressive kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: A multicenter retrospective study.
evidence.snippet: No patients permanently discontinued treatment due to toxicity-related events, and no drug-related deaths occurred.

evidence.reference_title: Sirolimus therapy for kaposiform hemangioendothelioma with long-term follow-up.
evidence.snippet: Mild side effects were observed.

evidence.reference_title: Pneumocystis Jirovecii Pneumonia During Sirolimus Therapy for Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma.
evidence.snippet: We report the case of a child with kaposiform hemangioendothelioma and the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon who developed Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia (PCP) while on sirolimus and a prednisolone taper, after lack of adequate response to prednisolone, propranolol, and vincristine.

evidence.reference_title: Pneumocystis Jirovecii Pneumonia During Sirolimus Therapy for Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma.
evidence.snippet: He had a prompt positive clinical and laboratory response to sirolimus, but 4 weeks after starting it, at the age of 4 months, he developed PCP. This led to respiratory failure, which required extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.

evidence.reference_title: Pneumocystis Jirovecii Pneumonia During Sirolimus Therapy for Kaposiform Hemangioendothelioma.
evidence.snippet: PCP is a rare but life-threatening side effect of sirolimus therapy, especially in the setting of concurrent steroid treatment. Pneumocystis prophylaxis should be considered for patients receiving sirolimus.

nodes.description: The cause of most tumours is unknown. A somatic activating GNA14 variant (c.614A>T, p.Gln205Leu) was found in one KHE in the 2016 discovery study, a finding the 2020 review gives as 1/3 of KHE specimens; a later sequencing series of five KHEs and two tufted angiomas found none. The mutations reported in KHE are sporadic, not germline. GNA14 belongs to the GNAQ family, whose G alpha subunits bind G-protein-coupled receptors. No cited source establishes the cell in which the variant arises within the tumour, so no cell is bound here. The node covers only tumours carrying the variant (one KHE in the cited studies), and even there the review leaves open whether it is a cause or a later change in the tumour.

evidence.reference_title: GNA14 Somatic Mutation Causes Congenital and Sporadic Vascular Tumors by MAPK Activation.
evidence.snippet: We found somatic activating GNA14 c.614A>T (p.Gln205Leu) mutations in one KHE, one TA, and one LCH and a GNA11 c.547C>T (p.Arg183Cys) mutation in two LCH lesions.

evidence.reference_title: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
evidence.snippet: Remarkably, the somatic activating GNA14 c.614A > T (p.Gln205Leu) mutation was found in 1/3 of KHE specimens and in 1/4 of TA specimens, although these studies were weakened by small sample size

evidence.reference_title: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
evidence.snippet: It is likely that the origin of KHE is multifactorial, with genetic factors being part of the contributing triggers, although the mutations in KHE tumor are sporadic rather than germline.

evidence.reference_title: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
evidence.snippet: In general, the etiology of KHE remains largely unknown.

evidence.reference_title: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
evidence.snippet: The GNAQ family encodes Gα subunits that form a heterotrimer with Gβ and Gγ subunits and bind G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs).

nodes.description: Complete resection is an option where it can be done safely; elective resection during the active Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon is ill advised. In one single-centre cohort, where over 90% were operated on, the authors favoured early surgery.

evidence.reference_title: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
evidence.snippet: Conversely, surgery can be an approach for tumors in which a complete and safe resection can be performed

evidence.reference_title: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
evidence.snippet: Elective resection of a KHE during the active phase of KMP is unusually not necessary and is ill advised.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment experience for different risk groups of Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.
evidence.snippet: Early surgical intervention may be the most definitive treatment option for most patients with KHE; multimodality treatment is the best choice for the extremely high-risk group.

nodes.description: At presentation in 56% of 107 patients in one series, and in 78% of 70 children in another (not stated as at presentation): the platelet trapping of the Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon.

evidence.reference_title: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: atypical features and risks of Kasabach-Merritt phenomenon in 107 referrals.
evidence.snippet: Common presenting features included enlarging cutaneous lesion (75%), thrombocytopenia (56%), and musculoskeletal pain or decreased function (23%).

evidence.reference_title: Treatment experience for different risk groups of Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma.
evidence.snippet: Common clinical characteristics included associated coagulation disorder (100%), locally aggressive cutaneous blue-purple mass (89%), thrombocytopenia (78%), and local pain or joint dysfunction (20%).

nodes.description: A vinca alkaloid. First-line vincristine has an overall response rate of 72%; in a multicentre cohort that pools KHE with tufted angioma, its radiological response at three months was higher than sirolimus's, with no difference at six.

evidence.reference_title: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: current knowledge and future perspectives.
evidence.snippet: First-line treatment with vincristine has an overall response rate of 72%

evidence.reference_title: Treatment practices and response in kaposiform hemangioendothelioma: A multicenter cohort study
evidence.snippet: The vincristine group had higher radiologic response at 3 months compared to sirolimus (72.7% vs. 20%, p = .03), but there were no differences between these groups at 6 months.
